status.comment: the contract between the engine and a project type; written 2026-09-09 from DESIGN-001 under the owner's rulings (the word is type; modules/vscode; a synthetic generic polygon; Theia from master as the second real type; types are separate packages from the start; the own root is a full path; no compatibility layer for the old configuration schema - the one consumer is migrated in the campaign). Implementation phases P1-P5 of the design.

p.TYPE-WHY: The engine of Codkit - patch sets, grafts, the own layer, the drift guard, `load`/`save`/`sync`, the generated branch, `cycle`, `rebase-onto-pin`, `publish`, licensing, standards delivery, the agent protocol - is universal. What is not universal is the knowledge of one family of upstreams: where own code lives, which file is the product manifest, how a service is overridden, how the tree is built and tested, which icons a distribution carries. Until now that knowledge sat inline in the engine and was VS Code's. A **project type** carries it instead, so that the same tool serves several VS Code forks, several Theia forks, and later products that are not IDEs.

facts.TYPE-TERM: A **project type** (short: type) is the tool's knowledge of one family of upstreams, shipped as one package and named by one identifier: `vscode`, `generic`, `theia`, later others. A patch set declares exactly one type. The engine asks the type; it never states a type's facts itself.
facts.TYPE-TERM-CAPABILITY: A **capability** is a named optional ability a type declares (`brand-images`, `gen-brand`, `build-channels`, `runtime-library`, `own-extensions`, `service-override`, `entry-module`, `config-overlay`, `dev-channel`, `upgrade-advisory`). A verb that needs a capability refuses when the type does not declare it (`TYPE-CAPABILITY-REFUSAL`).
facts.TYPE-TERM-PACKAGE: A **type package** is the npm package that implements a type against the contract package `@codkit/type-api`: `@codkit/type-vscode`, `@codkit/type-generic`, `@codkit/type-theia`. The tool repository is an npm workspace holding the CLI package and the official type packages side by side; each is published on its own at the development version 1.0.0 (`DEV-VERSION-IS-1-0-0`).

contract.title: 2. The contract: nine questions a type answers

p.TYPE-CONTRACT-IS-CLOSED: The contract is exactly the list of variation points measured in the engine (DESIGN-001 §1); a question is added to it only when a second type needs it, never in anticipation. Each area below is one object of small functions on the `ProjectType` interface of `@codkit/type-api`.

facts.TYPE-AREA-IDENTITY: **Upstream identity.** The tag pattern a pin may use, how a pin resolves to `tag@sha@date` (universal form), the fingerprints `check-tree` requires of a healthy tree (manifest name, marker files), the anchor policy.
facts.TYPE-AREA-LAYOUT: **Tree layout.** The own root (`typeConfig.ownRoot`, a path from the tree root: `src/vs/<name>` for VS Code, a workspace package for Theia), whether own extensions exist and where they materialize, the cleanup whitelist of build outputs the fresh pass may remove, the forbidden patch targets, type-specific marker comment forms if any.
facts.TYPE-AREA-LAYERS: **Layers.** `own`, `patch`, `resource-file` and `rewrite-rule` are universal and always present. `config-overlay` takes its targets and its optional dev channel from the type (VS Code: `product.json` with `product.overrides.json`). `own-extension` takes its materializer from the type (VS Code: `extensions/<name>`). `service-override` takes its verifier from the type (VS Code: `registerSingleton`; Theia: an inversify `rebind` in a container module). `entry-module` takes its locator from the type (VS Code: `workbench.common.main.ts`; Theia: the application's module list). A layer the type does not provide is absent for that patch set: `verify` refuses an artifact of that layer with `CK-E-TYPE-CAPABILITY`.
facts.TYPE-AREA-BUILD: **Build and test.** The dependency install, the hygiene and lint scripts, the compile channels behind `build up|down|status|errors` and the foreign-watcher markers, the test runner with an own-root glob, the package build and the stamps it needs. `ci --profile build` is one universal skeleton (PROP-011) whose steps call these answers.
facts.TYPE-AREA-ADVISORY: **Upgrade advisory.** The semantic readers the cycle runs between two pins (VS Code: built-in extensions of `product.json`, Electron and TypeScript versions). The advisory's frame - what changed, what it means, what to do - is the engine's.
facts.TYPE-AREA-BRAND-IMAGES: **Brand images** (capability `brand-images`). The target table of the distribution's icons and image forms; the generator, the index and the verifier are the engine's.
facts.TYPE-AREA-RUNTIME: **Runtime library** (capability `runtime-library`). Which shipped runtime package the type delivers with `codkit runtime load` (today's library becomes `runtime-vscode`).
facts.TYPE-AREA-STANDARDS: **Standards and skills.** The standard `minimal-intervention` is universal; the seam catalogue and the list "how upstream would build it" that `ck-intervene` routes through come from the type's packages (`seams-vscode`).
facts.TYPE-AREA-CONVENTIONS: **Conventions.** The subsystems of intervention ids, the forbidden service ids, the defaults of `conventions.json` a product may extend through `conventionsExtensionFile`; the marker grammar and the id pattern's shape stay the engine's.

p.TYPE-ENGINE-IS-BLIND: **What the engine never knows.** No module of the CLI package names a type's fact: no `product.json`, no `src/vs/`, no `extensions/`, no `registerSingleton`, no `npm run hygiene`, no icon table. The graft budget, the marker grammar, the drift guard's predicate, the sacrifice by name of `--discard`, the licence carriers, the generated branch, the cycle's transactions and the standards protocol belong to the engine and are forbidden to consult the type. A grep of the CLI package for the VS Code tokens of DESIGN-001 §1 is a gate of phase P2 and prints zero.

facts.TYPE-PACKAGES: Workspace layout of the tool repository: `packages/codkit` (the CLI and the engine; the binary `codkit`), `packages/type-api` (the contract), `packages/type-vscode`, `packages/type-generic`, `packages/type-theia`. Each package has its own `package.json`, tests and licence carriers; the floor runs over the workspace. The split happens once, in phase P2, and every later type is born as a package.
facts.TYPE-REGISTRY: The engine holds a **registry of the package names it will load**, keyed by type identifier (`vscode` → `@codkit/type-vscode`). A type is resolved by a dynamic import of that package from the CLI package's own dependencies; the official types are regular dependencies of the CLI package. No module is loaded from a patch set or from an arbitrary path: determinism, the air-gapped circuit and the clean room all want the set of loadable code fixed by the tool's own release. Adding a type is publishing its package and adding its name to the registry.
facts.TYPE-UNKNOWN: A `type` the registry does not know, or whose package is not installed, is `CK-E-TYPE-UNKNOWN`, exit 2, naming the identifier and the package the registry expected; no command proceeds without a type.
facts.TYPE-SUPPLY-KIT: The air-gapped supply kit (PROP-011) carries the CLI package and every official type package as tarballs; `npm pack` of the workspace produces them; the kit's manifest lists them with their versions and hashes.
facts.TYPE-API-STABILITY: `@codkit/type-api` is the only import a type package may take from the tool; the CLI package imports the type only through the interface. A change of the interface is a change of every official type in the same commit of the workspace (the workspace is one repository precisely so that this stays atomic).

facts.TYPE-CONFIG-FIELD: `codkit.json` schema 2 has `"type": "<identifier>"` and `"typeConfig": { ... }`. The engine validates the universal fields; the type validates `typeConfig` with its own schema and refuses with `CK-E-CONFIG` naming the field. One patch set, one type.
facts.TYPE-SCHEMA-2-REQUIRED: Schema 2 is the only schema: a `codkit.json` without `type` (schema 1) is refused with `CK-E-CONFIG` that names the two fields to add (`type`, `typeConfig.ownRoot`) and nothing else; no command reads schema 1 and no code path infers a type. There is one consumer of the tool today and it is migrated in the campaign (phase P2: its `codkit.json` gets `"type": "vscode"` and `"typeConfig": {"ownRoot": "src/vs/patchset"}`, and its gates - `verify`, `status`, `ci --profile build`, the static proof, the dev and package UI proofs - run on the migrated configuration). Owner ruling of 2026-09-09.
facts.TYPE-OWN-ROOT: The own root is a **full path from the tree root** in `typeConfig.ownRoot`; the field is required, the type supplies its constraints (VS Code: under `src/vs/`; Theia: a workspace package directory) and refuses a root outside them with `CK-E-CONFIG`. The engine treats the own root as an opaque directory: mirrored by content, excluded from the drift guard, named in the inventory.
facts.TYPE-MANY-FORKS: Several forks are several patch sets, each bound to its own fork tree per command (`--patches-dir`, `--fork-dir`, the local config), exactly as today (`GOAL-ANY-FORK`). Two forks of one upstream are two patch sets of one type; forks of different upstreams are patch sets of different types. Sharing between forks travels through packages (standards, runtime, skills), never through the tool's configuration. A workspace file naming several patch sets is a later convenience and is not part of phases P1-P5.

facts.TYPE-VERBS-UNIVERSAL: The verbs of the roster (PROP-007 `COMMAND-ROSTER`) are universal and keep their names, flags and exit codes. Their output names the type where it matters: `where` prints it, the JSON envelope carries `codkit.type`.
facts.TYPE-CAPABILITY-REFUSAL: A verb that needs a capability the type does not declare refuses with `CK-E-TYPE-CAPABILITY`, exit 2, naming the type and the capability, before any write; no verb silently does something else. The verbs that need one: `imageset *` (`brand-images`), `gen brand` (`gen-brand`), `build *` (`build-channels`), `runtime load|check` (`runtime-library`), and `verify` over an artifact of a layer the type does not provide.
facts.CMD-TYPES: `codkit types` - print the registered types, their package and version, and the capability matrix; `--json`: `data: {types: [{id, package, version, installed, capabilities}]}`. Read-only, no patch set required.
facts.TYPE-ERROR-CODES: New codes: `CK-E-TYPE-UNKNOWN` (type not registered or package not installed), `CK-E-TYPE-CAPABILITY` (verb or layer outside the type's capabilities). A type may add codes only under its own prefix (`CK-E-VSCODE-…`) for facts the engine cannot state; every code has an FAQ entry (PROP-012).

facts.TYPE-VSCODE: `vscode` - today's behaviour, extracted without change: the specification module `modules/vscode` holds its answers (layout `src/vs/<own>` and `extensions/`, the `product.json` overlay with the `product.overrides.json` dev channel, built-in extensions, `registerSingleton`, `workbench.common.main`, `npm ci`/hygiene/eslint/watch channels/`test-node`, the package build and its stamps, the advisory readers, the brand image set, the runtime library, the seam catalogue, the conventions). The product's gates - `verify`, `status`, `ci --profile build`, its static proof and UI proofs - are the regression net of the extraction.
facts.TYPE-GENERIC: `generic` - a plain git upstream with no product model: no extensions, no service overrides, no entry module, no dev channel, no brand images, no runtime library; the install, lint, compile and test commands are declared in `typeConfig`; the own root is a configured directory. It carries `own`, `patch`, `resource-file`, `rewrite-rule` and `config-overlay` over declared JSON targets without a dev channel, so that `load|save|verify|cycle|publish|ci` run over any upstream before its own type exists. Its polygon is a **synthetic repository** in the fixtures (owner ruling).
facts.TYPE-THEIA: `theia` - the second real type, designed from the facts of Theia master (`research/theia-facts-<version>`) and specified in `modules/theia`: the own root as a workspace package, the application manifest as the overlay target, inversify `rebind` as the service override, the application's module list as the entry module, yarn/lerna build and watch, its test runner, electron-builder packaging, its advisory readers. It is proved by a real product of the owner built on it, in that product's own repository, the way the VS Code product was built.

facts.TYPE-ENGINE-TESTS: The engine's tests run against a **stub type** in the fixtures that answers the contract with the smallest possible layout; they never import an official type. Each type package has its own suites and its own polygon; FEAT-001 becomes two polygons - the VS Code-shaped one it is today and the synthetic generic one.
facts.TYPE-SCENARIOS: Acceptance scenarios (FEAT-002): a schema-1 patch set is refused with `CK-E-CONFIG` naming `type` and `typeConfig.ownRoot`; the migrated VS Code patch set behaves exactly as before; `codkit types` lists the official types; `imageset` over a `generic` patch set refuses with `CK-E-TYPE-CAPABILITY`; a `type` the registry does not know refuses with `CK-E-TYPE-UNKNOWN`; the generic polygon passes `load`, `save`, `verify`, `cycle` and `ci --profile verify` end to end; the VS Code polygon passes every scenario it passed before the split.

facts.TYPE-SPEC-MODULES: `modules/codkit` specifies the engine and this contract; `modules/vscode` specifies the `vscode` type; `modules/theia` will specify the `theia` type; `common/*` states the vision without naming an upstream. A fact that is a type's answer moves to the type's module; a fact about the engine stays.
facts.TYPE-SPEC-TOMBSTONES: Anchors are immutable: a moved fact leaves a tombstone at its old address naming the new one (`NEVER-RENAME-OR-DELETE-A-CITED-ANCHOR`), and every `##ANCHOR` citation in code is re-pointed in the same commit; `trace:check` and the spec map are the gates. The unit count of the two modules together equals the count before the split plus the tombstones and the new facts of this document.
facts.TYPE-SPEC-LANGUAGE: The type modules of the tool are English like the rest of the tool's specifications (`SPEC-LANGUAGE-IS-ENGLISH`); a product's specifications keep the product's own rule.

p.DECISION-TYPE-IS-A-PACKAGE: **Decision:** a type is a separate npm package from the first day, resolved through a registry of names. **Why:** the owner's ruling - the procedure of splitting is done once; a package boundary that exists only in a directory drifts back into the engine. **Considered and rejected:** in-tree directories under one package (cheaper now, a second split later); arbitrary plugin loading from a patch set (breaks determinism, the air-gapped kit and the clean room). **When to revisit:** a third party ships a type - then the registry becomes a declared list in the tool's configuration rather than a constant.

p.DECISION-NO-COMPATIBILITY-LAYER: **Decision:** no compatibility layer for the old configuration schema: schema 2 is required, schema 1 is refused with a migration hint. **Why:** the owner's ruling of 2026-09-09 - the tool has one consumer, and fixing it is cheaper than building a compatibility layer and maintaining it afterwards; the consumer is migrated inside the campaign with its gates as the proof. **Considered and rejected:** reading schema 1 as `vscode` (a second code path, a second set of tests, and a rule that would outlive its only reason). **When to revisit:** never for schema 1; a future schema change gets the same treatment while the consumers can be counted on one hand.

p.DECISION-TYPE-CONTRACT-FROM-MEASUREMENT: **Decision:** the contract's areas are the measured variation points and nothing else. **Why:** an interface designed for one real type fits that type; the `generic` type and the Theia type are the two forces that keep it honest, and each new question is added when a type needs it. **Considered and rejected:** a general "hooks everywhere" plugin API (speculative surface, untestable). **When to revisit:** a third real type that needs a tenth question.
